source_refs.note: Isothermal Process: a main subheading of 6.4 First law of thermodynamics, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 126-126.

blocks.text: It is a process which is carried out at constant temperature and hence the condition for the application of Boyle's law on the gas is fulfilled. Therefore, when gas expands or compresses isothermally, the product of its pressure and volume during the process remains constant. If P₁, V₁ are initial pressure and volume whereas P₂, V₂ are pressure and volume after the isothermal change takes place (Fig. 6.7-a), respectively, then

blocks.text: Thus if gas expands and does external work W, an amount of heat Q has to be supplied to the gas in order to produce an isothermal change. Since transfer of heat from one place to another requires time, hence, to keep the temperature of the gas constant, the expansion or compression must take place slowly. The curve representing an isothermal process is called an isotherm (Fig. 6.7-a).
